pieces.title: Is your company a small business for tax? The $32 million test

content.text: Is your company a small business for tax? A business meets the small business gross receipts test for a tax year beginning in 2026 when its average annual gross receipts over the three prior tax years are $32 million or less; for 2025 the figure is $31 million.

captions.facebook:
Is your company a small business for tax?

A business meets the small business gross receipts test for a tax year beginning in 2026 when its average annual gross receipts over the three prior tax years are $32 million or less. For 2025 the figure is $31 million.

Gross receipts are the money a business takes in before any costs, and the test averages them over the three tax years before the one being tested.

pieces.title: Getting an EIN without a Social Security number

content.hook: Founder abroad with no Social Security number?
lines: An EIN is your company's federal tax ID number.
The IRS's online EIN application needs the responsible party's Social Security number or ITIN.
The responsible party is the person who controls the company, and an ITIN is an IRS tax number for individuals.
The online application is not open to a business whose principal place of business is outside the US.
A founder abroad who is not eligible for a Social Security number or an ITIN can still apply for an EIN on Form SS-4.
They write "foreign" or N/A on line 7b, as the form's instructions direct.
International applicants can get an EIN by phone on 267-941-1099 (not toll free), 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. Eastern, Monday to Friday.

pieces.title: QSBS: the $75 million line for stock issued after 4 July 2025

lines: QSBS is qualified small business stock.
For QSBS issued after 4 July 2025, the company's gross assets limit is $75 million.
That is up from $50 million for stock issued on or before that date.
4 July 2025 is the day the 2025 tax law was signed.
QSBS issued on or before 4 July 2025 must be held more than five years.
And if that stock was acquired after 27 September 2010, the exclusion, the part of the gain not taxed, can reach 100% of the eligible gain.

pieces.title: Non-accredited purchasers in a 506(b) round: what they must receive

content.text: Non-accredited purchasers in a 506(b) offering must receive disclosure documents generally the same as those used in Regulation A or registered offerings, including financial statements that in some cases may need to be certified or audited by an accountant.

captions.facebook:
Taking money from investors who are not accredited?

Under Rule 506(b), a company can sell to any number of accredited investors plus up to 35 other purchasers who are financially sophisticated, alone or with a representative. An individual can be an accredited investor through the SEC's income, net worth or license tests.

Non-accredited purchasers in a 506(b) offering must receive disclosure documents generally the same as those used in Regulation A or registered offerings, including financial statements that in some cases may need to be certified or audited by an accountant. Regulation A is a route for smaller public offerings, and a registered offering is one registered with the SEC.

pieces.title: Wyoming LLC: the annual report rule

content.text: Formed a Wyoming LLC? Its annual report isn't due on one date for everyone. A short thread on the rule, with an example.
thread: The rule: a Wyoming LLC's annual report is due on the first day of the month it was formed in, every year.

Worked example: an LLC formed in March has its annual report due on March 1, every year. Wyoming emails a courtesy reminder 60 days before the annual report is due, if the company has given the Secretary of State a current email address.
The cost: Wyoming's annual license tax is $60, or $0.0002 for each dollar of the company's assets located and employed in Wyoming, whichever is greater.
If it slips: a Wyoming company whose annual report tax is not paid within 60 days of the due date can be dissolved, and the reinstatement fee is $100.

pieces.title: Myth or fact: no Social Security number, no EIN

content.text:
Myth or fact: you can't get an EIN for your US company without a Social Security number.

Myth. A founder abroad who is not eligible for a Social Security number or an ITIN can still apply for an EIN on Form SS-4, writing "foreign" or N/A on line 7b, as its instructions direct.
thread: Where people get stuck: the IRS's online EIN application needs the responsible party's Social Security number or ITIN, and is not open to a business whose principal place of business is outside the US.

pieces.title: Form 1120: the deadline and the extension

content.text: Running a calendar year C corporation? One date and one form to put on your 2027 calendar now. A short thread.
thread: The rule: a calendar year C corporation's Form 1120 for 2026 is due by Thursday, April 15, 2027.
The extension: Form 7004, filed by that date, gives an automatic six month extension of time to file, to Friday, October 15, 2027.
Worked example: your C corporation runs on the calendar year. File Form 7004 by April 15, 2027, and the time to file its 2026 Form 1120 runs to October 15, 2027.

pieces.title: Delaware LLC: the $400 tax and its due date

content.text: Delaware LLC owners: your yearly state tax has its own amount and its own date. A short thread.
thread: The rule: a Delaware LLC pays an annual tax of $400, due by June 1 for the year before.
If it's late: a late Delaware LLC tax brings a $200 penalty plus interest of 1.5% a month on the tax and penalty.
Worked example: an LLC that owes the tax for 2026 pays its $400 by June 1, 2027. Paid after that, the $200 penalty and the 1.5% a month interest are added.
Compare: Delaware corporations file their annual report and pay franchise tax by March 1 each year; in 2027 that is a Monday.
